name: Hearth Circuit — The Meridian Home Cook Competition
creator: Produced by Orisun Media (Tier 3 independent broadcaster)
description: Hearth Circuit is Meridian 88's longest-running food competition broadcast, operating since 2191 on a biannual format: sixteen home cooks from across all tiers compete across six challenge rounds judged by a rotating panel of food critics, community figures, and — controversially — a standing AI palate judge called the Arbiter, whose scoring has been disputed in three separate seasons. The show's format explicitly pairs competitors from different tiers and requires cross-tier collaboration rounds, which has produced both genuine friendships and some of the most uncomfortable broadcast moments in Meridian food media. Broadcast via neural feed with a physical studio audience of 200; the prize is Φ12,000 and a one-year residency at a licensed commercial kitchen.
cultural_impact: Hearth Circuit has an unusually loyal multi-tier audience because it is one of the few broadcast formats where Tier 1 and Tier 2 contestants regularly win — the judging criteria explicitly weight resourcefulness and flavor innovation over ingredient cost. Three former contestants have gone on to open restaurants that became significant cultural institutions.
controversy: Season 14 (2218) was nearly cancelled after the Arbiter AI gave a Tier 1 contestant's synth-protein fermentation dish a score of 2.1/10, a result widely perceived as algorithmically biased against low-cost ingredients. The backlash prompted an independent audit of the Arbiter's training data, which found it had been weighted toward Tier 4-5 dining standards.
story_hooks: A Tier 1 contestant in the current season is cooking dishes that incorporate techniques from the Ferment Underground's supply chain — and someone on the production team has noticed the gray-market ingredient sourcing.
The Arbiter AI's audit revealed bias, but the full audit report was never released publicly; a journalist has obtained a copy suggesting the weighting was not accidental.

A former Hearth Circuit winner who opened a Tier 2 restaurant on their prize residency has been quietly bought out by a corponation food subsidiary — and they're about to appear as a guest judge on the current season.
